sentences.text: Alarm indications are assessed according to protection significance, equipment condition, and the potential effect on service.
The Control Room Operator reviews the alarm priority, source, time, and associated bay indications before deciding on a response.
The operator distinguishes a new alarm from a standing condition and checks whether related indications support the same assessment.
For a protection operation or an unexplained equipment state, the Control Room Operator treats the condition as requiring prompt investigation.
The Control Room Operator acknowledges alarms only after reviewing the indication and retains awareness of any condition that remains unresolved.
The Control Room Operator uses the acknowledgement slip to record the alarm response and any outstanding action.
The operator checks available device status and sequence information without treating a cleared indication as proof that the underlying cause has been corrected.
The Feeder Protection Relay indication is reviewed against the affected feeder status and any related protection operation.
The Bay Automation Controller provides bay-level status indications that support the operator’s assessment of the alarm.
Glasswing shall retain alarm state and event information for operator review after an indication has cleared.
The Sequence Event Archive provides time-ordered evidence for later operational review.
The North Protection Panel contains the protection equipment associated with feeder protection functions.
The Control Room Operator uses indications from the North Protection Panel to assess feeder protection operations and related alarms.
The Transformer Protection Panel is dedicated to protection functions associated with the power transformer rather than feeder protection.
The Transformer Protection Panel provides local indication of transformer protection operation for assessment during an alarm response.
The Control Room Operator considers the condition of the Station DC System when alarms or protection indications suggest a possible control-power concern.
A breaker status discrepancy is treated as an abnormal condition until its cause and operational significance are understood.
The Engineering Workstation is used for authorized review of protection and event information, not as a substitute for immediate operational assessment.
The Protection Relay Engineer supports investigation when relay indications, settings concerns, or event evidence require technical interpretation.
The Substation Field Crew confirms device identity and local conditions before carrying out an authorized operation.
The Substation Supervisor is consulted when the alarm response requires escalation beyond routine operator actions.
The Control Room Operator produces the Clearance Handoff Memo when an unresolved alarm condition requires a formal handoff.
The Switching Desk Coordinator confirms operational handback before the associated state-change evidence is considered available for authorized engineering review.
After handback, the Control Room Operator verifies that alarm status, equipment status, and recorded evidence are consistent before closing the response.
